blind_spots_patched: The baseline dossier omitted $15.5B in off-balance-sheet endorsement contract obligations (~$1.7B due in 12 months), $7.3B in product and other purchase obligations, $3,091M–$3,179M in balance-sheet operating lease liabilities (which flip Nike from headline net cash to $2.01B–$2.70B lease-adjusted net debt), 2025 credit rating downgrades by S&P and Moody's, $1.1B in supplier finance payables, and the unresolved Belgian Customs appellate duty claim.

Chapters 1–6 omitted NIKE's dual-class voting structure (Class A electing 8 of 11 directors via Swoosh, LLC's 78.8% Class A stake), executive PSU metrics tied to Adjusted Revenue and Adjusted EPS rather than ROIC/FCF, and November 2026 governance/accounting turnover (Dan McKenzie returning as CAO after CFO Denton served as Interim Controller, Mónica Gil's Nov 19 resignation, and Alexandre Arnault joining the Compensation Committee).

Chapter 3 detailed footwear factory concentration but omitted apparel supplier concentration (64 manufacturers, top 6 supplying ~54%, Vietnam 34% / Cambodia 15% / China 12%), 205 strategic Tier-2 raw-material suppliers, internal Air Manufacturing Innovation dependence for Air-Sole components, and confirmation that no single customer exceeded 10% of FY2026 revenue.

Beyond U.S. IEEPA tariff refunds, the baseline dossier missed the unresolved Belgian Customs duty appeal (dating to FY2018 imports, backed by bank guarantees) and NIKE's twice-yearly standard FX rate accounting mechanism that routes actual-vs-standard currency variances and derivative hedge gains/losses into Corporate.
assumptions_changed: WEAKENED: Hill's 'Win Now' and 'Pace' reset stabilized FY2026 revenue at $46.4B and is positioned to drive near-term operating margin recovery toward double digits.

CONFIRMED: North America wholesale rebounded +9% in Q1 FY2027 and the $986M FY2026 Q4 IEEPA tariff recovery booking ($684M receivable at May 31, 2026) would convert cleanly to cash.
